findings.title: Fee is modeled both as extra ledger entries inside the peer transfer (design §9.1 step 8) and as a separate 'fee'-type transfer (schema §1 and transfers.type enum); the two models conflict and the fee-type transfer has no defined flow

Reconciliation check (c) stored-vs-computed balance depends on unpinned system-account seed balances/opening entries; if nonzero or mismatched it reports false positives and breaks AC-6's 'exactly 3 problems'. Also the HELD->FAILED release path is silent on balances.

Top-up and withdraw require an Idempotency-Key and insert idempotency_keys.user_id (non-null FK), but their bodies carry no user id and the path-wallet->owning-user mapping that scopes the key is unspecified
findings.location: design.md §9.1 step 3, §8 API table, §11; schema.md idempotency_keys.user_id

findings.title: Insert-first idempotency relies on blocking at the UNIQUE INSERT only; the design references 'replaying an in_progress key' (§17) without stating the negative invariant that no code path SELECTs an in_progress row to decide a replay

Reconciliation is specified at REPEATABLE READ but never states it tolerates concurrent live transfers (check (c) correctness under concurrent commits); AC-6 only tests a quiescent DB, leaving an undocumented operational constraint

Naming drift between from_account_id/to_account_id (schema) and from_wallet_id/to_wallet_id (API body and a design §14 index) with no stated wallet-id->account-id mapping; both FK columns are nullable with no flow that produces NULL

Deferred per-transfer balance CONSTRAINT TRIGGER (§9.1.3) is described as evaluating 'once per transfer touched', but a Postgres constraint trigger fires FOR EACH ROW; the stated granularity is imprecise and could lead to a non-working implementation choice

AC-1 stampede (100 rapid withdrawals from one wallet) assumes 'exactly 50 succeed' but the pinned seed enables velocity (hold) and rapid_drain (flag) rules which such a burst would trip; AC-1 and AC-9 share one seed with conflicting fraud expectations and no pinned thresholds
findings.location: design.md §12 AC-1, §12 AC-9, §14 Part A, §9.1 step 6

findings.title: Reconciliation should state that the job_locks SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT is the first statement in the REPEATABLE READ transaction so a losing contender fails fast before opening a snapshot
idempotency_keys.body_hash typed as 'BYTEA/CHAR(64)' either/or in schema §2 while §11.1 pins CHAR(64) lowercase hex; pick one to avoid a migration mismatch
Fee amount is said to live 'in config/risk_rules' but risk_rules has no fee column and 'fee' is not a valid action (hold|flag); where the fee amount is stored is under-specified for migration 0014
